## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this search yet. Earlier searches ran 84 trials, and every one scored 0 on both dev and training success, so no idea has any evidence behind it. Training success was also 0, which means the agent never completed an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. The shaping reward can be gamed: a 2x2 brick with 3 correct cells and 1 wrong cell earns the same as an exact 1x2. Only the +1 terminal bonus rewards exactness, and the agent rarely reaches it. This round covers the untested directions in breadth, each stacked with others. Every candidate uses PPO initialisation hygiene, a skip carrying raw observation channels into the head (through a learned 1x1 layer), and factorised logits. Beyond that they differ in recipe extremes, normalisation, trunk shape, and three new head types: a soft-AND over footprint cells, soft landing-layer attention, and dense/global heads. Any score above 0 is a real signal.

### Round 2
Round 1 had 6 trials, and every one scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That adds to the 84 earlier zeros. These trials tried hygiene init, GroupNorm, a raw-obs skip, factorised logits, a soft-AND head, a soft landing-layer head, long-credit recipes, and 426k steps at lr 3e-3. None of them helped. Because training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build even on the data it trains on. So the bottleneck is optimisation, inductive bias, or a hidden world quirk (layout, footprint or gravity), not generalisation. I have no positive evidence, so this round goes for breadth. The six candidates test: the legality mask as input combined with a wide 5x5 per-type head (robust to a shifted layout); a U-Net trunk with a down-sampled global path; many small updates; a low-entropy, small-clip recipe that commits early; an MLP-Mixer trunk with layout-free token mixing; and an everything-plausible stack. All keep r at or below about 1.45 and use mostly 1 epoch, which buys more fresh samples.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0, on dev and in training. Before this search, 84 more trials also scored 0. Trunks, heads, init, norms and recipes all failed in the same way, so the blocker is probably shared, not a missing piece of perception. My hypothesis is a do-nothing trap. Early on, random placements mostly fill cells outside the target, so their reward is negative, while DONE returns exactly 0. DONE therefore gets a positive advantage, and since it is a single logit it learns faster than any placement skill. The policy collapses to stopping early, episodes become short, and later build states are rarely visited. An earlier DONE bias of -2 is overridden quickly and does not test this. This round tests ways to stop the collapse: a soft cap on all logits (which bounds p(DONE)), a bounded stop gate, and a slowly learned DONE. Each sits on a different trunk and recipe. If all six still score 0 in training, the hypothesis is refuted.

### Round 4
After 17 trials, only one has scored above 0: r3c3 (soft cap 3, dilated (1,2,1) GroupNorm trunk, 2 epochs, gamma 0.99). It scored 0.002 on dev, which is 1 of 512 designs. Its training success was still 0. That is very weak evidence and may be luck, but it is the only signal we have. Every other family scored 0, including the other soft caps (2 and 2.5, both 1 epoch), U-Nets, stop gates, Mixers, recipe extremes and everything-stacks. This is the last round, so all 6 slots go near r3c3, following the program:
- a near-copy at slightly different width, to check it was not luck;
- four variants that each change one thing: cap 4, wider dilation, 1 epoch for more fresh samples, and a DONE head that also reads skip features;
- one stack of those changes.

If none of them scores above 0, r3c3's result was probably seed noise. The real blocker is then still unknown: training success never left 0, so the agent never completes exact builds even on its own training designs.
